summary: Whether Containment Protocol ("negate all activated and triggered effects") can negate the trigger-like attributes ({Alluring}, {Resonant}) was asked in a RAQ thread and never answered. Caleb answered only the Crevice Lurker half (the tax). The owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“{Resonant} is its source's trigger: damage…”) states that Containment Protocol can negate a {Resonant} rider, and the engine negates a waiting {Alluring} trigger.

sides.quote: Whether Containment Protocol ("triggered effects") negates trigger-like attributes.
my intent is for it to stop those from triggering
Crevice Lurker taxes it, and Containment Protocol can negate it.
Negate all activated and triggered effects.

resolution: An open thread is not a ruling. The rule follows the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“{Resonant} is its source's trigger: damage…”) and the engine (they are put on the stack as triggered abilities, so they can be negated), which is consistent with Caleb's answer on the tax. Revisit if the thread is answered.

summary: A RAQ follow-up asks whether a static that removes attributes (Monke) also removes attributes a unit gains after it began to apply, and was never answered in its thread. The answered thread says only that such statics affect units entering play later. The engine lets an attribute gained later (a Powerful virus) stand.

sides.quote: _passer's follow-up: does Monke's static (unlike a resolved Suppression Field) strip attributes a unit gains later?
Monke and Transmogrifant have Static Abilities meaning they work continuously and affect new units entering play
RAQ Transmogrifant: an attribute a unit gains AFTER it is in play is not affected

resolution: The rule states only what the answered thread says (it applies to units entering later, and ends when the static leaves). How a later grant interacts with the static is a timestamp question for rule 709; the open follow-up is recorded, not answered.

summary: When two effects could each replace or redirect the same event, only one applies. No printed or designer source says which one; the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“the REPLACEMENT-EFFECT LAYER: two families, and…”) takes the first in entity order ("ties break by entity id"), an engine choice.

sides.quote: the first claimant takes it and ties break by entity id, exactly as `replaceRotDamage`
Ask the player now
its a replacement effect so it just takes one thing and replaces it with another (you the player control how they stack)

resolution: Answered by the owner on 2026-10-16: asked who orders replacement effects whose order changes the outcome, he chose "Ask the player now", after Caleb (rules-questions 2025-11-25): "you the player control how they stack". The player the event affects chooses the order (effects.replacement.once.one-applies); the entity-id order is retired, and with two Counter Thieves the counters end on the second to apply ("On the second Thief").

summary: The order "add, then double" is the designer's for damage and {Powerful} (the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“Additive damage modifiers apply before {Powerful}…”), from the RAQ). For a life-total multiplier (Arbiter of Vitality) beside an additive modifier, the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“multipliers are exponential (round-32 Q4)”) says the composition is still unruled and the engine's order is an interim decision.

sides.quote: > "Bellowing Boulder with Powerful and Conduit of Pain: (1+1)x2 damage to each unit =
**⚠ THE ADDITIVE COMPOSITION IS STILL UNRULED, and Q4 asked about it.** R157 §23
Conduit of Pain adds its 1 BEFORE Powerful doubles
generally as the owner of all the replacement effects, you can choose the order you'd like to apply them in
which usually would mean doing +1 then doubling
For cases where its "just worse" *give them the option* to choose, but be like "Yo, this will be a higher number".

resolution: Settled on 2026-10-25. Caleb (rules-questions 2026-02-23): "as the owner of all the replacement effects, you can choose the order you'd like to apply them in", "which usually would mean doing +1 then doubling" "for max damage" — for damage and for a life multiplier alike. The owner (replacement order Q4/Q5) keeps the choice and makes the higher number a one-click default; between players, Q1 "Each owner, INT first". effects.replacement.multipliers.additive-first, concepts.damage.amount-order and attr.powerful.additive state it; the engine asks (699).

summary: Sources silent on two prevention effects on one unit (two Phytochemical Protections). The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“PREVENTED damage was never dealt […]”) says nothing in the corpus addresses it; the engine treats the second as re-applying the first, so the unit gets one counter per damage prevented, not two.

resolution: No rule is written for the case. Recorded so a judge does not read the engine's behaviour as a rule.

summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“The static → effect-attribute channel (EffectAttrMod)…”) is presented as current, but its "OPEN" section says the engine computes the {Resonant} rider from the undoubled amount and that this was deliberately not changed. The owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“{Resonant} is its source's trigger: damage…”) later made the rider damage from the source, so {Powerful} doubles it (the RAQ's 2/4 Powerful Resonant deals 8 to the face). The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“The static → effect-attribute channel (EffectAttrMod)…”) carries no partial-supersession mark.

sides.quote: ### ⚠ OPEN — the RESONANT rider is doubled twice in the RAQ, once in the engine
So everything that prices damage from that source prices the rider: {Powerful}

resolution: The rule follows the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“{Resonant} is its source's trigger: damage…”). Mark the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“The static → effect-attribute channel (EffectAttrMod)…”)’s "OPEN — the RESONANT rider" section as superseded by the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“{Resonant} is its source's trigger: damage…”) in the register. [The ruling register this refers to was retired on 2026-10-11; its owner calls now live in the rule records.]

summary: The owner ruled that several Wraith deployment triggers may "target the same unit" and the surplus fizzles. The owner ruling of 2026-08-24 (“deployment uses the stack, and a…”) reads "target" as an aim chosen when the trigger goes on the stack, which can fizzle, but not as a real target: it fires no "when I become targeted" ability and cannot be redirected.

sides.quote: > stack simultaneously and be allowed to target the same unit, even exceeding
R144 grants **1 and 2** — which is exactly and only what the owner asked for —

resolution: Settled by printed text: the Wraith prints "put a -1/-1 counter on an ally", not "target ally", so the choice is not a target and fires no "when I become targeted" ability. The owner ruling of 2026-08-24 (“deployment uses the stack, and a…”)’s "target the same unit" is loose wording for what the owner asked (several Wraiths may choose one unit, and the surplus fizzles). The rule states that. Since 2026-10-16 the owner's call is that the Wraith's choice is not a target and is made as the trigger resolves, so it no longer fizzles while an ally is in play (concepts.targets.not-target.wraith, effects.triggered.chosen-unit); the 2026-08-24 call quoted above is history.

summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“the REPLACEMENT-EFFECT LAYER: two families, and…”)’s owner sentence names only 'When'/'Whenever' and colons as what reaches the stack, but the Manual's timed triggers ('After combat'), the trigger-like attributes (owner ruling of 2026-10-09, “{Resonant} is its source's trigger: damage…”) and a targeted replacement's substitute (owner ruling of 2026-08-23, “a REPLACEMENT may put a triggered…”) also reach the stack. The sentence is a heuristic, not an exhaustive list.

sides.quote: > effects that go onto the stack are cards that say 'When' or 'Whenever' or have
Triggered abilities may also take place at specified times,
Crevice Lurker taxes it, and Containment Protocol can negate it.

resolution: Printed text and the later rulings extend the owner's heuristic; the rule lists all of them. No owner question.
